 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C. V. Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.32108 of 2015
Order:
This Writ Petition is filed praying this Court to declare the action of the respondents in not paying
the compensation amount under Award No.04/2013-2014 dated 30.12.2013 (

Sathupalli Mandal, Khammam District as arbitrary, illegal, irregular and also against to the principles of natural justice and in violation of Article 14, 19 and 300-A of Constitution of India
and consequently, direct the respondents to immediately pay the compensation and implement the R&R Policy to the petitioners.
2. The case of the petitioners is that the 1st petitioner is the wife and the 2nd petitioner is the daughter of late Vaikunta Rao who died on 25.02.2012 in a road accident.

It is the case of the petitioners that late Vaikunta Rao was the owner and possessor CVBR, J wp_32108_2015 of the house site admeasuring Ac.0-03 cents in R.S.No.45 and also an agricultural land admeasuring Ac.01-00 cents in R.S.No.59 situated at Kommepalli Village, Sathupalli Mandal, Khammam District having acquired the said property in the partition among his brothers and father and the revenue authorities also mutated his name in the revenue records and issued pattadar pass book and title deeds in his favour.

It is the further case of the petitioners that after the death of her husband, the 1st petitioner requested the 5th respondent to mutate her name in the revenue records, but he has been dragging the matter on one or other reason.
It is the further case of the petitioners that their land was acquired for the purpose of JVR Open Cast-II for mining in Kommepalli Village, Sathupalli Mandal.

In pursuance of the request made by the 6th respondent, the 3rd respondent has issued notices under the Land Acquisition Act and after following the procedure he passed Award No.04/2013-2014 dated 30.12.2013 and determined the compensation payable in respect of the acquired lands.

3. The grievance of the petitioners is that even after passing the said award, the respondents have not deposited the CVBR, J wp_32108_2015 compensation amount and also not extended the Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy to them.

4. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent No.3 has placed before this Court the written instructions vide Rc.No.C/134/2/2008 dated 01.10.2015 issued by the Special Deputy Collector (LA), IPT & Railways, Khammam; wherein it is stated that after following the procedure an award was passed for the extents of the lands of the petitioners vide award No.04/2013-14, dated 30.12.2013 and thereafter, notice as required under Section 11 (1) of Bimala Lakshmi, W/O Late Vaikunta Rao, vs The State Of Telangana Rep. on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92168557/
1 the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short "the LA Act, 1894") was issued by fixing the market value @ Rs.2,12,000/- per acre.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further stated that an extent of Ac.0-03 cents in Survey No.45 has not been acquired as claimed by the petitioners and an extent of Ac.5-05 guntas in Survey No.59 of Kommepalli Village has been acquired as per the award proceedings dated 30.12.2013.

Since the land losers have not cooperated for award enquiry, the land compensation and tree value of the award has been ordered to be deposited in the Court of Senior civil Judge, Sathupalli under Section 31(2) of the LA Act, 1894 read with Section 30 of LA Act, 1894 for CVBR, J wp_32108_2015 deciding the title and payment of compensation.
It is also stated that the petitioners are not entitled for extending the benefits under the Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners by placing reliance on the policy laid down in G.O.Ms.No.68, dated 08.04.2005, claims that the petitioners are the Project Displaced Family on account of losing valuable rights over their lands and hence, they are entitled for the benefits of the Rehabilitation and Resettlement policy.
6. In view of the above submissions, since there is no dispute that the petitioners are the Project Displaced Family, this Court deems it appropriate to dispose of this writ petition directing the respondents to examine the claim of the petitioners for extending the benefits under G.O.Ms.No.68,
Irrigation & CAD (Project Wing-LA-IV-R&R) Department, dated 08.04.2005, if they are otherwise eligible under the said G.O.
7.
With the above observations, this Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.

CVBR, J wp_32108_2015 As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
_________________________________ JUSTICE C.V. BHASKAR REDDY Date:
